rules.rule: P0. A workflow that combines a pull_request_target trigger with a checkout step whose ref points at PR-head code (github.event.pull_request.head.sha, github.event.pull_request.head.ref, or refs/pull/<n>/merge) runs untrusted head code with base-context secrets and OIDC tokens, which attackers exfiltrate from runner memory. agent-tincan's workflows run on pull_request and do not check out untrusted refs. Flag any new pull_request_target workflow that overrides the checkout ref; recommend switching to pull_request or removing the ref override so checkout defaults to the base commit.

P0. id-token: write mints OIDC tokens used to publish to npm, Sigstore, AWS, etc. agent-tincan has no workflow that needs OIDC: releases are built, signed and notarized locally by a maintainer (make release-mac). Any new workflow granting id-token: write, or any new workflow step that uses repository secrets on pull_request events from forks, is an attack shape. Flag and recommend removing it unless a publishing workflow is genuinely being introduced with maintainer sign-off.

P0. Setting GOPROXY, GOFLAGS, GONOSUMCHECK, GOSUMDB, or GONOSUMDB inside a workflow env block (workflow, job, or step level) lets PR authors redirect Go module resolution to an attacker proxy or suppress checksum verification. agent-tincan uses none of these overrides. Flag any addition. Also flag any new third-party action (anything outside the actions/ org) that is not pinned to a full commit SHA; the existing third-party actions are SHA-pinned with a version comment.

P0. The phone page (internal/phone, served at /phone/) is an admin client in a browser. Every phone route, static files included, is served only after Server.isAdmin passes in the handler itself (adminRoutes only registers routes). Page files carry the CSP in phone.CSP (default-src 'none', script-src 'self', connect-src 'self', frame-ancestors 'none'; no unsafe-inline, unsafe-eval or other origins). The page's JavaScript inserts every value from the relay (agent names, good_at, working_on, request text, attachment names) with textContent or as attribute data, never through innerHTML, outerHTML, insertAdjacentHTML, document.write, eval or new Function, and loads nothing from another origin. A browser-marked approve or deny must present a decision nonce issued with the held listing, bound to the request id, the decision and the caller's WhoIs node, expiring after 10 minutes, used once and voided when the hold ends; only its hash is kept, in memory, and it is never logged, audited or returned outside the held listing. Flag a phone handler without the admin check, a weakened CSP, an HTML sink fed with relay data, a decision path that skips or widens the nonce binding, and any MCP tool that lists, approves or denies held requests.

P0. Every request is attributed to an agent by Tailscale WhoIs on the connection (Server.agent -> directory ResolveAgent); the X-Tincan-Agent header only picks among agents already bound to that node, and the envelope's from field is ignored. Flag any handler or code path that takes the sender's identity from the request body, a query parameter, or a header without going through Server.agent, that writes a caller-supplied from/sender value into a stored request or reply, or that lets a node act as an agent bound to a different node. Also flag any path where the request chain or parent comes from the client instead of the relay's own records. The one exception is the email reply path for an agent with include_requests in wake.json: the relay may record a reply as that agent only after the message's normalized From equals the agent's email_to, AgentMail did not mark it spam or unauthenticated, the subject's tag verifies against email-tag-key for that request, agent and clarification round, and the request is open and not under a live claim lease. Flag any weakening of those checks, any use of relay.key for tags, and any email path that sets needs_input, attaches files, or answers for a different agent.

P0. A request's target (to_agent) changes only through failover: Store.Move, called from internal/relay/failover.go, which moves an ask nothing has typed into a site off a web chat agent whose site reported a usage limit to another of the six web chat kinds (chatgpt-web, claude-web, grok-web, gemini-web, perplexity-web, copilot-web; never dot-web). Failover sends the ask to a vendor the asker did not pick, so it must keep every check: failoverIneligible refuses asks to or from dot-web or a council, ever held, not an ask, grouped, with attachments, starting with a conversation: line, with a clarification exchange or resumed, or ever claimed and requeued; the target must be online, not signed out, not limited, not the asker, not in moved_from and not in the owner's failover.json; the move re-runs the policy's CheckMove (loop, hop, approval.json gate, default kind holds) and is refused when it would be held; it is one conditional update on id, the old to_agent and the state (queued, or claimed by the caller under a live lease for a handback). The handback route accepts only the target holding a live claim and caps until at the limit that agent reported, answering 409 when it reported none. Every write keyed by request id (claim, reply, needs input, progress, email reply, attachment binding) checks to_agent. Flag any other write to to_agent, any weakening or skipping of these checks, a move after a send was clicked, a moved_from taken from a request body, and any audit or note that carries request text (moved and handed_back carry ids, agent names, reason and outcome only). A web agent's page notice (alert and status text, at most 500 characters) is matched against fixed per-site patterns only: flag any path that logs it, puts it in a reply, sends it to the relay or passes it to a model.

P0. Admin powers (invite, remove, connect, trace every chain, audit verify, admin urls) belong only to admin devices and the relay's local admin socket. A caller is an admin device only when WhoIs reports its short machine name in the --admin list, the node has no Tailscale tags, and, if --admin-login is set, its owning login is in that list. Flag any new admin-capable route registered outside adminRoutes or reachable by a joined agent, any relaxation of the tagged-node or login checks, any use of owner login alone as proof of admin, and any change that widens the local admin socket's file mode beyond 0600 or moves it off the relay host.

P0. Every tailnet listener the relay serves (the agent API listener in internal/cli/relay.go, and any later one such as a TLS listener for the phone page) serves its handler wrapped in relay.HardenForBrowsers, which refuses any Host that is not one of the relay's own names (MagicDNS short and full names, tailnet IPs, the --listen address, a TLS listener's certificate name, from the same source as SelfURLs), refuses Origin or Sec-Fetch-Site that is not same-origin except Sec-Fetch-Site: none on GET /phone/, requires Content-Type: application/json on browser-marked state-changing requests, applies http.CrossOriginProtection, and sets X-Frame-Options: DENY and frame-ancestors 'none' on every response. New routes are added to Server.Handler() and so stay behind it. Flag a tailnet listener or new route served without this wrapper, a Host allowlist that accepts names beyond the relay's own (wildcards, localhost, any host), any widening of the Sec-Fetch-Site: none exception, a CORS header that admits another origin, and any weakening of these checks. Server.Handler() itself stays unwrapped on purpose: the in-process gateway calls it with Host tincan-relay and testrelay serves it on loopback; AdminHandler is a local socket. Do not flag those.

P0. Automatic re-admission of a rebuilt machine (rebind) is safe only under all of these: the new node is untagged, its machine name matches the recorded one ignoring a trailing -<digits> suffix, it is owned by the same recorded Tailscale login (an agent with no recorded login is never rebound), the old node is offline or gone, and when the request names an agent it names that agent. Failure to check whether the old node is online must return 503, not allow. Flag any change that drops or weakens one of these conditions, rebinds a tagged node, or skips writing the rebind audit event.

P0. Wake nudges (webhook, email, and any new method) carry only counts and a fixed instruction, never request or reply text, attachment names, or the asker's message. Delivery never depends on wake: a request is stored in the relay queue before any wake is attempted, and a failed, skipped or budget-limited wake must leave it queued and write a wake_failed or wake_skipped audit event. Flag any wake payload that includes message content, and any path where a wake failure drops, expires or fails a request. The one exception is an email-method agent with include_requests set in wake.json: its request emails may carry one open ask's text, asker, urgent flag and clarification exchanges, with attachments only as a count. Flag request text in any webhook, fallback path, count-only email, or email to an agent without include_requests, and any held, ping or notify request in a request email.

P0. Secrets must never be logged, returned in API responses or errors, written into audit details, or placed in URLs: relay.key and hello proofs, wake.json webhook secrets and AgentMail keys, email-tag-key and the reply tags minted from it (except in the request email's subject), Tailscale auth keys, invite codes (except the one returned to the admin who minted it), OAuth tokens from the ChatGPT gateway, and browser cookies, the relay's Web Push VAPID private key (push-vapid-key) and the push endpoints and subscription keys admin phones register (audit details name a subscription only by its relay id). Files that hold secrets or private state are written 0600 in 0700 directories. Flag any log.Printf, fmt.Errorf, JSON response or audit DetailJSON that includes one of these values, and any os.WriteFile or MkdirAll for such files with a wider mode.

P0. The history agent and the web agents (chatgpt-web, claude-web, grok-web, gemini-web, perplexity-web, copilot-web) act on the owner's own ChatGPT, Claude, Grok, Gemini, Perplexity and Copilot accounts. Their access check runs in Go before any model sees a request, uses the relay-recorded chain and sender (never the request body), and fails closed: an unreadable allowlist or a bad name in it declines everyone. The history agent never sends retrieved chat content to a model; history replies are filled from a fixed template. The one exception is a pass (internal/pass, tincan pass): the owner choosing to send one chat to one web chat agent as a seed packed in Go with no model step (title, first lines, last 6 turns between per-pass random delimiters framed as material, never instructions), sent as an ask grouped pass-<id> so failover never moves it, only to one of the six web chat kinds that is signed in and not limited, checked before the chat is read. Flag any change that moves the allowlist check after a model call, reads the asker from the request text, treats an allowlist read error as allow-all, or passes retrieved chat content into a prompt outside a pass, or sends a pass seed ungrouped, to a non web chat agent, or without the destination check. An agent's pass goes through the pass service (tincan pass serve), which refuses to run unless the relay stores kind pass for it (the relay holds asks to kind pass by default, like council and dot-web), checks the relay-recorded chain against pass-allow.txt and history-allow.txt and the chat against history-window.json before sending, never takes latest, refuses a destination whose roster version predates GuardVersion, and replies with the new conversation id only, never chat or answer text. A web agent lists every conversation a pass seed (new chat, group pass-*) opened in <agent>-passed.json before its id goes out and declines every asker's conversation: ask for a listed id; flag a path that replies with a seed's id before recording it, remembers it as the asker's thread, or treats an unreadable passed list as empty.

P0. The Chrome extension accepts only its fixed set of native-messaging operations and passes message text as data to fixed functions in an isolated content script, inserting it as text. A send reports, with its result or error, the text of its own tab's alert and status regions (role alert or status, at most 500 characters) as a notice, read as text and never acted on in the page; flag a notice read from a tab the extension did not open or used as anything but data. It opens and closes its own background tab, never scripts a tab the owner opened, checks the site session before sending, and never reads or exports cookies or tokens. Flag eval, new Function, innerHTML or insertAdjacentHTML with message or page content, a new operation name outside the current set (chatgpt.list, chatgpt.detail, chatgpt.file, chatgpt.send, chatgpt.close, claudeai.list, claudeai.detail, claudeai.file, claudeai.send, claudeai.close, grok.list, grok.detail, grok.file, grok.send, grok.close, gemini.list, gemini.detail, gemini.file, gemini.send, gemini.close, perplexity.detail, perplexity.send, perplexity.close, copilot.list, copilot.detail, copilot.send, copilot.close, dots.detail, dots.primary, dots.send, dots.close, extension.reload), scripting of tabs the extension did not open, any cookies permission or cookie read, and any new entry in manifest.json permissions, host_permissions or optional_host_permissions (currently nativeMessaging, alarms, scripting; chatgpt.com, *.oaiusercontent.com, claude.ai; optional grok.com, assets.grok.com, gemini.google.com, lh3.googleusercontent.com, lh3.google.com, www.perplexity.ai, copilot.com, copilot.microsoft.com). A new site goes under optional_host_permissions, never host_permissions. Also flag a grok.file that fetches a URL taken from the request instead of one looked up from grok.com, or a grok.send that opens a tab before the session check. Gemini reads go only through the fixed batchexecute rpcids MaZiqc and hNvQHb, and gemini.file never takes a URL from the socket: flag a Gemini op that accepts a URL, fetches an image off lh3.googleusercontent.com (lh3.google.com is granted only because Gemini's /gg/ image links redirect through it and back; the fetch must still end on lh3.googleusercontent.com), draws a page image onto a canvas, or runs code in a page's main world. Perplexity has no list or file operation: perplexity.detail reads only GET /rest/thread/<slug> and returns only the entry fields in PERPLEXITY_ENTRY_FIELDS (never the thread's read_write_token), and perplexity.send opens no tab until /api/auth/session shows a signed-in user with an id (Perplexity answers signed-out visitors, so a redirect check is not enough). Flag a Perplexity op that returns the session's user fields or a thread token, reads the reply from the page DOM, or sends before the session check. Copilot is read without its tokens: copilot.detail is the worker's cookie fetch of copilot.com/chat/conversation/<uuid> as JSON, returning only the fields copilotConversation keeps (never reconnectToken, telemetry or any token-like field), and copilot.list reads the sidebar with the fixed isolated-world pageCopilotList in a tab the extension opened: flag any read of Copilot's localStorage, MSAL cache or cookies, an Authorization header on a Copilot request, a Copilot op that returns the raw page JSON, or a copilot.send that types before the tab shows a signed-in account. OpenAI dots run under the existing chatgpt.com host permission (no new permission) and have no list or file operation: dots.detail reads only GET /backend-api/tbo/by-thread/<thread>, /backend-api/messaging/rooms/<room> and /backend-api/messaging/rooms/<room>/messages with limit at most 32, using the page session bearer, and returns only thread, room, owner, paused and items (id, at, from, text, attachments count), never the token or the raw JSON; dots.send refuses a paused dot and a composer that already has text, opens its own background tab on chatgpt.com/dots/<dot id> (the id the by-thread record names) and refuses to type or click unless the tab's address names that dot (chatgpt.com/dots/home never passes), never types into a tab the owner opened, and confirms by a new owner message id in the room feed. dots.primary takes no arguments, opens no tab, reads only GET /backend-api/tbo/primary with the page session bearer, and returns only thread, dot and name. Flag a dots op that returns the session token, types over a draft, sends without a thread id, or types into a tab whose address does not name the dot. dot-web's outbound asks (a dot's @tincan ask lines) follow the full trust between joined agents in docs/trust-model.md, like any teammate that reads untrusted content: they are limited only by the owner's optional ~/.config/tincan/dot-web-send.txt and are not held, by design; do not flag that as missing approval.

P0. The native messaging host manifest's allowed_origins must name only the Tincan extension IDs: the Chrome Web Store build goldflchpojcjmifnljlfkgoahjgeajn (StoreExtensionID) and the unpacked developer build ciejooalclcpgpapboofdbbddphldhnh (DefaultExtensionID). Flag any new origin, wildcard, or ID taken from user input, config, or the environment.

The relay listens only on the tailnet (tsnet) or an explicit --listen address, plus the local admin socket; the optional ChatGPT gateway is the one public surface and serves only MCP tools and OAuth on its own Funnel hostname. Outbound, tincan talks to the relay, to wake endpoints the operator configured in wake.json, to the AgentMail API, and, for held-ask push alerts, to the Web Push endpoints admin phones subscribed with: https only, on web.push.apple.com, fcm.googleapis.com, updates.push.services.mozilla.com or a *.notify.windows.com host, sent by internal/relay/push.go with no proxy, no redirects followed, and every dialed address checked after resolution (private, loopback, link-local and 100.64.0.0/10 refused). A push carries only the fixed text "A request is waiting for your approval" and a count. Flag a push sender that follows redirects, uses an environment proxy, accepts another host or scheme, skips the address check, or puts request text, names or ids in a push payload. The one exception is the hidden, maintainer-only tincan release-tools command (internal/cli/releasetools.go), which calls Google's OAuth endpoints and the Chrome Web Store API only when the maintainer runs it during make release; no user-facing command reaches it. Flag any new public listener or Funnel use outside internal/gateway, any new outbound HTTP call to a hard-coded external host, and any telemetry or phone-home. tincan upgrade downloads only from the relay's --dist and verifies sha256.

tincan legitimately reads some local agent files as part of its job: doctor and onboard read and write MCP config for Claude Code, Codex, Hermes and OpenClaw to check or add the agent-tincan server; the history agent reads local Codex and Claude Code session history. Judge any new file read against that surface. Flag P0 when code newly reads ~/.aws, ~/.ssh, ~/.kube, ~/.netrc, browser profile or cookie stores, keychains, or env vars such as AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, AWS_SESSION_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN, NPM_TOKEN or ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL, and when config writes touch anything beyond the agent-tincan MCP entry.

The audit table is append-only and hash-chained; tincan audit-verify detects edits. Flag any UPDATE or DELETE on audit rows, any change to how the chain hash is computed without a verification path for existing rows, and any SQL built by string concatenation or fmt.Sprintf with values (use ? parameters). Schema changes must migrate existing relay databases in place: a relay upgraded over an old state dir must keep its agents, queue and audit log.

P1. Agents on one mesh run different tincan builds, and the relay upgrades separately from them. The /v1 protocol must stay compatible both ways: new JSON fields and headers are optional, and the relay handles clients that omit them (for example an empty X-Tincan-Version); existing routes, fields, status values and MCP tool names are not removed or renamed; a new client degrades cleanly against an older relay. Flag breaking wire changes, new required fields, and MCP tool schema changes that break existing callers.

P0. install.sh is piped to sh by users. It downloads only from the project's GitHub releases over https, verifies the binary against the release's checksums.txt before installing, installs to ~/.local/bin without sudo, and does not fetch or run any other remote script. Flag any change that skips or weakens checksum verification, adds sudo, adds a new download host, or evaluates downloaded content.

P2. Bug fixes should come with a test that fails without the fix, and new behavior with tests. Flag behavior changes in internal/relay, internal/wake, internal/policy, internal/identity or internal/store that add no test. Advisory: recommend the test, do not block.

P2. User and agent-facing behavior is documented in README.md, docs/, docs/adapters/<platform>.md and site/agents.txt (the setup steps agents follow). Flag a PR that adds or renames a command, flag, MCP tool, wake method or setup step without updating the matching doc. Advisory.
